market_mistake: The market prices the SCALED HYPERSCALERS as the parties that capture the layer below the model. This card's claim is about ATTRIBUTION WITHIN that layer, not about whether the layer captures at all: if frontier capability commoditizes, the scarce assets are the compute SOLD and the interconnection OWNED, and those are held in part by neoclouds and owners of powered infrastructure that the market prices as financing vehicles rather than as parties capturing economics. BOUNDARY, DECLARED: 'scaled hyperscaler' here means MSFT, AMZN and GOOGL BY NAME. The boundary is written down because ORCL sits on it — the parent sheet has ORCL owning hyperscale infrastructure, and in this scan ORCL grades QUANTIFIED-REVENUE-SHARE, a HIGHER disclosure tier than any of the big three. Under the narrow boundary the claim is merely softened; under a boundary that admits ORCL the claim is PARTLY INVERTED, because a member of the set said not to disclose does disclose, above the neoclouds it is contrasted with. The narrow boundary is the one that preserves the claim, which is precisely why it is stated here as an operator call rather than assumed silently. OPERATOR TO RULE — if ORCL is inside, this card is REDRAWN, not edited. THE DISCLOSURE ASYMMETRY IS NOT THE EVIDENCE, AND ITS CAUSE IS NOT STRUCTURAL. The prior draft claimed the asymmetry had an innocent structural cause — hyperscalers fund from operating cash flow and so have no occasion to publish contract-level economics. The 745-name scan FALSIFIES that: ORCL and BABA both reach quantified-revenue-share while running cloud at scale. Quantifying cloud AI economics is possible at scale; the big three's aggregation is a CHOICE, not a structural necessity. That retraction changes nothing about the guardrail it was attached to. 'Choice, not structure' does NOT license inferring attribution from the FORM of disclosure — that is the same absent-evidence error wearing a new justification. Every party here discloses under its own incentive, and those incentives are STRUCTURED, not free: neoclouds publish binding contracts because the contract is the collateral they finance capex against; SIX OF THE NINE binding-tier names are crypto-mining operators pivoting to AI hosting, carrying a further incentive to publish contracts as proof the pivot is real; ORCL and BABA quantify where quantifying helps them; incumbents stay aggregate for competitive reasons. Disclosure form measures INCENTIVE, never economics. CONSEQUENCE: the big three's AI-compute economics are NOT MEASURABLE from their filings, in either direction — the absence is not evidence for the claim and its retraction is not evidence against it. That is why this card rests on CONVERSION at a name that reports both sides, and never on who publishes a contract.
null_thesis: The parties the market already favours are the parties that capture it: the neocloud contracted backlog proves to be a financing artifact that does not convert to recognized revenue at the contracted duration, and owners of land, substation and grid interconnect are repriced as landlords rather than as holders of the scarce asset. The attribution claim is wrong and the market's existing attribution is right.

first_confirming.trigger: At the next quarterly print of CRWV — the one name in the cohort that reports both sides — REVENUE RECOGNIZED AGAINST PRIOR-PERIOD REMAINING PERFORMANCE OBLIGATIONS rises, or the RPO-to-revenue duration SHORTENS. Accumulation is not the test: a backlog that never converts still grows, so 'contracted backlog grows' is consistent with this thesis and its null simultaneously. CONVERSION is where the two diverge.
first_confirming.basis: one full scheduled print cycle; CRWV already discloses both RPO and recognized revenue ($60.7bn RPO at 2025-12-31 against $15.1bn a year earlier), so both sides of the ratio are published line items. Deliberately ONE NAME and ONE RATIO: an OR across five names is near-certain to trigger on something, which is a test that cannot fail.

falsifiers.trigger: Recognized revenue against prior-period RPO FALLS, or RPO-to-revenue duration LENGTHENS, across two consecutive prints — the backlog is accumulating without converting, which is the null's own signature.
falsifiers.basis: two-plus scheduled print cycles of a disclosed ratio. PROPOSED — operator to select.

falsifiers.trigger: Counterparty concentration breaks the cohort: a named counterparty behind the binding contracts insources or cancels, and the contracted backlog is revealed as one customer rather than a market. BLZE's case already rests on a single contracted counterparty.
falsifiers.basis: disclosed counterparty concentration + contract amendments. PROPOSED — operator to select.

falsifiers.trigger: The frontier-to-open catch-up window WIDENS past ~6 months, removing the premise this driver INHERITS from ai-value-migration: if frontier capability does not commoditize, the scarce asset never moves down to compute at all.
falsifiers.basis: inherited premise, not this card's own claim. PROPOSED — operator to select.

CORRECTION LOG (2026-09-02, second pass — the first draft's four failures are kept below rather than overwritten): the prior draft's INNOCENT STRUCTURAL CAUSE for the disclosure asymmetry is RETRACTED. ORCL and BABA both grade quantified-revenue-share while running cloud at scale, so quantification at scale is possible and the big three's aggregation is a choice. The guardrail it was attached to SURVIVES the retraction and is restated in market_mistake: choice-not-structure still does not license reading attribution off disclosure FORM. FUNNEL, 745 graded: 404 aspirational-intent / 203 no-exposure-disclosed / 127 committed-capacity-or-capex / 9 binding-contract / 2 quantified-revenue-share. MSFT, AMZN and GOOGL all land at committed-capacity, driver-specific and unquantified, now measured with Google INSIDE the population. FOUR DEFECTS IN THE BINDING TIER, none yet closed: (a) CONFOUNDED — six of the nine (BTBT, CIFR, RIOT, WULF, plus the pivoting remainder) are crypto-mining operators moving to AI hosting, a cohort with its own incentive to publish contracts as proof the pivot is real; the tier therefore selects for disclosure incentive at least as strongly as for economics. (b) DOUBLE-COUNTED — BTBT holds ~70.5% of WYFI, so the tier is EIGHT assets, not nine. This was flagged once already on the parent sheet and reappeared here, which makes it a scan-time defect rather than an adjudication slip. FIXED AT SCAN TIME: `flag_intra_population_control` now flags any pair where one scanned issuer discloses majority control of another scanned issuer, on BOTH rows. It FLAGS and never drops — which side of a control pair carries the exposure is an adjudication. Verified against both live archives (745 and 241 rows): finds exactly BTBT/WYFI, no false positives, and would have caught it on the FIRST scan. Its RECALL IS LOW and the flag is not a clean bill: disclosed_facts are driver-exposure extracts rather than the filing, so a control relationship surfaces only where it was relevant to the driver AND the subsidiary was cited exchange-qualified — true of 2 of 745 rows. The complete source is EDGAR Exhibit 21 (Subsidiaries of the Registrant), not extracted anywhere in this repo yet. A pair this misses the analyst owns. (c) UNSTABLE — the tier churned between runs under an unchanged taxonomy: HUT out, BTBT/CIFR/RIOT in. That is not merely 'the count carries no weight'; it means the tier is not yet a stable measurement, and no claim may rest on its membership until two consecutive runs agree. (d) UNMEASURED — `machine_grade` classifies the FORM of evidence and never its SIZE, and no materiality gate exists. PRE-REGISTERED GATE, set BEFORE the next run and recorded here so it cannot be tuned after: to reach binding-contract or quantified-revenue-share a fact must carry a DISCLOSED ABSOLUTE MAGNITUDE of at least USD 100m (contract value, committed capex, or annualized recognized driver revenue); a fact with no number cannot reach either tier at any size. Basis for the floor: the cohort's largest disclosed commitment is CRWV's $60.7bn RPO, and a floor ~2.5 orders below it is permissive enough not to select for the answer while excluding lines that cannot move a layer measured in tens of billions. DISCLOSURE ON THE PRE-REGISTRATION: it is not clean — DUOT's $18.8m of prepayments against $32,549 of recognized revenue and HUT's ~1,100 GPUs with no disclosed revenue were both already seen when the floor was chosen. What the floor was NOT set from is the distribution of the other seven, which has not been tabulated. The operator can judge the contamination because it is written down; the number is a rule about materiality to a LAYER, not a cut placed between two observed groups. FIRST DRAFT'S FOUR FAILURES (recorded, not discarded): (1) it put rhetorical weight on a count of seven binding names, but the grade classifies form and not size — DUOT is $18.8m of prepayments against $32,549 of recognized hosting revenue and HUT is ~1,100 GPUs with no disclosed revenue, both binding and both economically trivial. The count is gone from the claim; the claim rests on conversion. (2) two of the seven (WULF, APLD) are not in the parent's 357-name universe, so the draft compared two populations while reading as one. (3) GOOGL's absence was reported as a FINDING when it was a TOOLING DEFECT: every prefilter term was observer vocabulary ('hyperscaler', 'neocloud', 'IaaS') rather than the words a hyperscaler uses about itself, so a scan of the compute layer excluded Google Cloud — a hole exactly where the counter-evidence would sit. Self-description terms were added; all three scaled clouds now clear. (4) the first-confirming could not fail — 'contracted backlog grows' is satisfied by the null as well as the thesis. Re-cut on conversion, one name, one ratio. Also on the operator's ruling: mechanism is valuation-dislocation, not supply-side (the supply-side premise is inherited and appears as falsifier 3); the null's fourth clause was CUT as the parent's; and the EQIX boundary is declared at CLASS level in the DriverSpec (owns the interconnection in, leases the space out), which governs adjudication at worksheet time and does NOT change scan-time tagging — EQIX and DGXX still return mixed ties and are resolved by hand.
